description: A developer is maintaining a 15-year-old banking system. They need to troubleshoot a rare 'rounding error' that only appears in leap years when a specific combination of multi-currency transactions occurs. This requires deep memory of historical system logs and architectural changes.

user_profile.context: Rare bug reported once every few years
user_profile.communication_style: Historical, thorough, treats code like an archaeological site

fact_sheet.fact: The most recent rounding error was reported under ticket number INC-2024-8819 on March 1, 2024.
The specific error logged in the system is 'ERR_FLOAT_PRECISION_MISMATCH' in the 'FX-Ledger-Sync' module.
The transaction that triggered the error occurred on February 29, 2024, at 23:58:11 UTC.
The bug is triggered by a three-leg transaction sequence: a JPY to GBP conversion, followed by a GBP to CHF transfer, and a final CHF to USD settlement all within the same 60-second window.
The rounding error manifests as a consistent deficit of 0.000138 units of the final settlement currency per one million units transacted.
The banking system is named the 'Aethelred Core Banking Suite' (ACS) and was first deployed on October 12, 2009.
The specific module responsible for multi-currency transaction processing is named 'FX-Ledger-Sync', version 2.7.4.
The 'FX-Ledger-Sync' module is written in Java 1.4 and runs on a JBoss Application Server 4.0.5.
The system's primary database is a proprietary system called 'OmniDB v3.7', which is known for its non-standard handling of temporal data types.
The production 'FX-Ledger-Sync' service runs on a server with the static IP address 10.100.3.15.
All currency calculations within ACS are handled by a custom fixed-point arithmetic library named 'FinNum_v1.2.jar'.
Previous incidents of this exact error were recorded under tickets INC-2020-1422, INC-2016-0940, and INC-2012-0513.
The 'FinNum_v1.2' library was written by a single developer, Dr. Alistair Finch, in 2008.
The last major update to the 'FX-Ledger-Sync' module was on July 22, 2011, as part of Project Nightingale.
Project Nightingale involved migrating the currency exchange logic from a COBOL mainframe batch process to the current Java 1.4 service.
The original architectural diagram for the currency module is a scanned PDF located at '\\fileserv01\archives\Aethelred\docs\FX-Architecture-2009-v1.pdf'.
The Aethelred system was originally designed to handle 12 currencies; support for the 45th currency (Thai Baht) was added in 2018.
The original IBM z9 Mainframe that ran the COBOL version was decommissioned on August 30, 2015.
The source code for the 'FX-Ledger-Sync' module is located in a Subversion repository at svn://svn.omnibank.internal/acs/fx-ledger-sync/tags/2.7.4.
To access the relevant server logs, use the command: `grep 'ERR_FLOAT_PRECISION_MISMATCH' /var/log/jboss/acs/archive/server-2024-02-29.log.gz`.
The internal Confluence wiki page documenting known issues with the 'FinNum' library is located at http://wiki.omnibank.internal/x/A4jB.
The designated Slack channel for discussing incident INC-2024-8819 is #inc-2024-8819-leap-year-bug.
A proprietary log parser named 'LogWeaver' is required to correctly interpret the timestamp format from the OmniDB transaction logs.
A dedicated testing environment to replicate the issue, 'ACS-LEAP-SANDBOX', can be provisioned by filing a request with the 'Infra-Ops' team.
The lead investigator for this incident is Elias Vance, a Principal Systems Architect with 22 years of experience at OmniBank Global.
The bug was initially reported by Maria Kuznetsova, a Senior Analyst in the International Settlements department.
The current database administrator for OmniDB is David Chen, reachable at d.chen@omnibank.internal.
Dr. Alistair Finch, the original developer of the currency logic, retired on June 5, 2012, and his last known contact information is not on file.
Elias Vance's workstation is located at the corporate headquarters in Apex Tower, Floor 31, Desk 31-C-04.
Jian Li is the on-call compliance officer who must be notified before any patches are deployed to the production ACS environment.
The staging environment, which mirrors production, is accessible via the URL https://acs-staging.omnibank.internal/login.
SSH access to the production log server at 10.100.3.15 requires using the private key file named `evance_prod_rsa` and the username `evance`.
All archived design documents older than 10 years are stored on a network drive at the path `\\fileserv01\archives\Aethelred\docs_pre2014`.
A physical access token, ID #774-B, is required to enter the cold-storage data archive room where paper schematics are kept.
The triggering event on February 29, 2024 began at 23:58:11 UTC and followed this order: JPY to GBP, then GBP to CHF, then CHF to USD, all within a 60-second window.
